Insulators and Boilermakers — Building Systems

Insulators Local 16 and Boilermakers Local 549

Insulators Local 16 and Boilermakers Local 549 apprenticeship and training, OSHA 29 CFR 1926.1101 asbestos in construction, 29 CFR 1910.146 permit-required confined spaces, ASME Section I and Section IX, and the National Board Inspection Code (NBIC), as taught across mechanical insulation, firestop, abatement, boiler and pressure-vessel repair work

Stations across the two trades that keep a plant's pipes, walls and pressure equipment doing what they are rated for: pipe insulation and jacketing, a firestopped penetration, an asbestos glovebag removal, a boiler tube rolled and welded back in, a pressure vessel entered and hot-worked, a furnace wall relined in castable, a repair proven on a hydrostatic test, and a mechanical room sprayed in foam behind a respirator that was actually fit-tested first.

20 / 20levels at 75+ lessons
1693lessons across the track
120tasks: a station under a condition
0more stations needed to fill it

Every level reaches 75 lessons. A lesson is one station step run under one condition; each level's number is its tasks' steps added up from the station modules.

The ladder

Level 1 is open; each level opens when the one below is passed — every task in one run of it a mastery run. A task opens its station with its condition; the number after each task is its steps.

Building Systems & Facilities

Mechanical Insulation, Pipe and Jacketing

13 steps · 4 hazards · 2 interruptions · par 5 min · indoors

A hot process pipe only gets insulated and jacketed once the bare metal's surface temperature is proven safe to touch, because the burn hazard under an unfinished run is invisible to anyone judging it by eye alone.

  • ANSI/ASSP — ANSI/ASSP A10.8 — Scaffolding safety requirements
  • union — Insulators Local 16 — heat and frost insulators and allied workers apprenticeship and training, as a training body
  • OSHA — 29 CFR 1910.1000 — Air contaminants and the permissible exposure limits
  • OSHA — 29 CFR 1910.134 — Respiratory protection
  • OSHA — 29 CFR 1926.451 — Scaffolds, general requirements

Firestop and Fire Wrap Installation

14 steps · 4 hazards · 2 interruptions · par 5 min · indoors

A wall or floor opened for someone else's pipes and cables only goes back to being a rated assembly when it is closed to the exact listed system the annular space and the penetrant mix were tested against, not to whichever detail looks close enough.

  • ANSI/ASSP — ANSI/ASSP A10.8 — Scaffolding safety requirements
  • union — Insulators Local 16 — heat and frost insulators and allied workers apprenticeship and training, as a training body
  • NFPA — NFPA 51B — Fire Prevention During Welding, Cutting and Other Hot Work
  • OSHA — 29 CFR 1910.1000 — Air contaminants and the permissible exposure limits
  • OSHA — 29 CFR 1910.1200 — Hazard communication
  • OSHA — 29 CFR 1910.134 — Respiratory protection

Building Systems & Facilities

Asbestos Glovebag Removal on a Pipe

14 steps · 4 hazards · 2 interruptions · par 5 min · indoors

Stripping asbestos pipe insulation inside a sealed glovebag while the header stays in service means the seal is proven before a single strip, because a contained job and a fibre release inside that same bag are separated only by whether the bag actually holds.

  • EPA — 40 CFR Part 61 — National Emission Standards for Hazardous Air Pollutants, including the asbestos NESHAP
  • union — Insulators Local 16 — heat and frost insulators and allied workers apprenticeship and training, as a training body
  • NIOSH — NIOSH criteria documents, Health Hazard Evaluations and the Pocket Guide to Chemical Hazards
  • OSHA — 29 CFR 1910.1000 — Air contaminants and the permissible exposure limits
  • OSHA — 29 CFR 1910.1200 — Hazard communication
  • OSHA — 29 CFR 1910.134 — Respiratory protection
  • OSHA — 29 CFR 1926.1101 — Asbestos in construction

Building Systems & Facilities

Boiler Tube Replacement and Rolling

14 steps · 4 hazards · 2 interruptions · par 5.3 min · indoors

A failed firetube only gets replaced by rolling the new stub to a specified expansion and welding it clean, and the drum only closes again once a foreign-object walk proves nothing was left inside it to travel loose at pressure.

  • ASME — ASME Boiler and Pressure Vessel Code, Section I — Rules for Construction of Power Boilers
  • ASME — ASME Boiler and Pressure Vessel Code, Section IX — Welding, Brazing and Fusing Qualifications
  • union — Boilermakers Local 549 apprenticeship and training, as a training body
  • NBIC — National Board Inspection Code, maintained by the National Board of Boiler and Pressure Vessel Inspectors — inspection, repair and alteration practice for boilers and pressure vessels in service
  • OSHA — 29 CFR 1910.147 — The control of hazardous energy (lockout/tagout)

Pressure Vessel Confined Entry and Hot Work

14 steps · 4 hazards · 2 interruptions · par 5.3 min · indoors

Welding a patch inside a vessel means the confined-space permit and the hot-work permit are read as one job, because an atmosphere proven safe and a fire watch posted are both preconditions for the same few minutes of work, not separate boxes to check.

  • ASME — ASME Boiler and Pressure Vessel Code, Section IX — Welding, Brazing and Fusing Qualifications
  • union — Boilermakers Local 549 apprenticeship and training, as a training body
  • NFPA — NFPA 51B — Fire Prevention During Welding, Cutting and Other Hot Work
  • OSHA — 29 CFR 1910.146 — Permit-required confined spaces
  • OSHA — 29 CFR 1910.252 — Welding, cutting and brazing, general requirements

Building Systems & Facilities

Refractory and Castable Installation

15 steps · 4 hazards · 2 interruptions · par 5.3 min · indoors

A furnace wall relined in castable is only as sound as the anchors it was poured over and the dryout ramp that follows, because rushing either one bakes a weak spot into a lining nobody can see the inside of once it cures.

Building Systems & Facilities

Hydrostatic Test and Inspector Witness

15 steps · 4 hazards · 2 interruptions · par 5.3 min · indoors

A repaired vessel is proven safe by a hydrostatic test only when the trapped air is vented before the fill, the walk for weeps happens from beside every joint rather than in front of it, and an inspector actually witnesses the hold.

  • ASME — ASME Boiler and Pressure Vessel Code, Section I — Rules for Construction of Power Boilers
  • union — Boilermakers Local 549 apprenticeship and training, as a training body
  • NBIC — National Board Inspection Code, maintained by the National Board of Boiler and Pressure Vessel Inspectors — inspection, repair and alteration practice for boilers and pressure vessels in service
  • OSHA — 29 CFR 1910.146 — Permit-required confined spaces
  • OSHA — 29 CFR 1910.147 — The control of hazardous energy (lockout/tagout)

Spray Foam and Respirator Fit

14 steps · 4 hazards · 2 interruptions · par 5.3 min · indoors

Spraying closed-cell foam next to an open isocyanate drum only starts once the respirator has been quantitatively fit-tested on the person wearing it, because a mask nobody has proven seals is a hope, not a control.

What it proves

Competency: Insulate, firestop, abate, repair and pressure-test a plant's pipes, walls and vessels to code

Demonstrated with a mastery run on 4 of its 8 stations, against OSHA 29 CFR 1926.1101 Asbestos in construction; OSHA 29 CFR 1910.146 Permit-required confined spaces; ASME Boiler and Pressure Vessel Code.

Badges

Each passed level earns an Open Badges 2.0 assertion naming the level, its tasks and their conditions, its lessons and the standards it evidences, with the attempts behind it as evidence, and sends an xAPI statement. Passing level 20, the capstone, climbs the whole track.

A run demonstrates mastery when it earns two or more stars, records zero unsafe actions, answers every interruption it was given, and finishes within 1.5 times the station's par time. One mastery run on enough of a competency's stations earns "demonstrated"; mastery runs on three different days earn "consistent". No other rule earns a competency.

Certification the work leads to: Insulators Local 16 and Boilermakers Local 549 apprenticeship and training, OSHA 29 CFR 1926.1101 asbestos in construction, 29 CFR 1910.146 permit-required confined spaces, ASME Section I and Section IX, and the National Board Inspection Code (NBIC), as taught across mechanical insulation, firestop, abatement, boiler and pressure-vessel repair work. No level claims apprenticeship hours: no registry entry states an equivalence.

Generated from the programme's station modules: lesson counts are read, not typed. The rules are in tools/briefs/ladder-brief.md and the full table in docs/ladders.md.
